title: The Mishra Family Is Back. Gullak Season 5 Drops on SonyLIV Tomorrow, and for NRIs, It Might Be the Most Important Show of the Week.
excerpt: TVF's quiet masterpiece about middle-class India returns with new family pressures, a recast eldest son, and the same emotional precision that has made it essential viewing for homesick diaspora audiences.
body:
There is a certain kind of Indian show that doesn't trend on social media, doesn't generate fan wars, doesn't have a cinematic universe or a post-credit tease — and yet, when a new season drops, a very specific demographic clears its evening. *Gullak* is that show. Season 5 arrives on SonyLIV on June 5, and for a significant section of the Indian diaspora, it might be the week's most meaningful release.

This is not an exaggeration. *Gullak*, created by The Viral Fever and now in its fifth season, has built its reputation on something that most Indian content platforms have abandoned in their chase for scale: specificity. The Mishra family — parents Santosh and Shanti, sons Annu and Aman — live in a small-town home that could be any home in the Hindi heartland. Their problems are not cinematic. EMI payments. A son who needs to prove himself. A wife who manages the household's emotional infrastructure while pretending she is only managing the kitchen.

## What's New in Season 5

The new season introduces a significant shift. Annu Mishra, the elder son, is now played by Anant Joshi, replacing Vaibhav Raj Gupta who carried the role through the first four seasons. Recasting a beloved character is a risk for any show, but *Gullak*'s strength has always been its ensemble — Jameel Khan as Santosh and Geetanjali Kulkarni as Shanti remain the show's anchors, and early reviews suggest the family chemistry has survived the transition.

The season explores Annu's growing desire to move out of Mishra Niwas and into his own apartment — a narrative thread that will resonate with anyone who has navigated the fraught Indian calculus of independence versus family obligation. When does leaving home become abandonment? When does staying become stagnation? These are questions that Indian families have argued about at dinner tables for generations, and *Gullak* treats them with the seriousness they deserve.

Aman, the younger son played by Harsh Mayar, is reportedly carrying secrets of his own this season. And the arrival of Shanti's brother Pinky, played by Gopal Datt, adds an outsider's perspective to a household that has learned to communicate in half-sentences and loaded silences.

## Why NRIs Keep Coming Back

For Indian diaspora audiences, *Gullak* operates on a frequency that most streaming content cannot reach. It is not aspirational. It is not escapist. It is a mirror held up to the homes they left behind — the specific texture of middle-class Indian life that cannot be replicated in an apartment in Jersey City or a townhouse in Brampton.

The show's power lies in its details. The way Shanti covers the good sofa cushions with a cloth when guests are not expected. The arithmetic Santosh does before ordering a second dish at a restaurant. The unspoken hierarchy of whose TV preferences take priority after dinner. These are not plot points. They are the connective tissue of an entire way of life, and for people living thousands of miles from it, watching *Gullak* is less entertainment than it is emotional maintenance.

Sunita Rajwar and Helly Shah join the cast this season, with directors Shreyansh Pandey and Abhay Raut taking over from Palash Vaswani, who helmed the first four seasons. The directorial change is notable but not alarming — TVF's house style tends to be consistent across its shows, and the writing team remains the primary creative force.

## The Streaming Landscape Needs This

*Gullak* Season 5 arrives during a week that also brings *Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge* to JioHotstar, *Maa Behen* to Netflix, and *Brown* to ZEE5. In that lineup, it is the smallest show with the quietest marketing. It does not have a ₹1,100-crore theatrical run to boast about. It does not have a star cast that fills magazine covers.

What it has is five seasons of earned trust with an audience that values emotional honesty over spectacle. For NRI families who will watch it together on a laptop screen in a living room that smells nothing like the one they grew up in, that trust is worth more than any opening-weekend number.

*Gullak* Season 5 streams on SonyLIV from June 5. All episodes will be available at launch.
